title: More warm surface in airflow
hook: Change surface area and predict convective heat rate.
misconception: convective heat rate stays fixed when surface area doubles.
objective: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT to compare convective heat rate when surface area changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed convection coefficient and surface-to-fluid temperature difference, Q̇ = hAΔT. When surface area doubles, convective heat rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = hAΔT; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed convection coefficient and surface-to-fluid temperature difference, with a nonzero initial result. If surface area triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on convective heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = hAΔT under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
